headline: GOLD BLASTS THROUGH $4,400 — TOUCHES $4,421 INTRADAY AT 10-WEEK HIGH; CPI WEDNESDAY SETS NEXT $150 MOVE
snippet: Gold broke through $4,400 per ounce during U.S. trading on August 10, touching an intraday high of $4,421.50 — its highest level since early June 2026 and a 10-week high — before settling near $4,409. The advance extends last week's $300 payrolls-driven surge (July nonfarm payrolls -23,000 vs +180,000 consensus) and marks a qualitative change in the rally: gold has now fully recovered from the June–July correction and closed above the critical 52-week moving average two consecutive sessions. Silver pushed to $66.41 on August 11, a 3.9% single-day gain from Friday's $63.80 close as the gold-silver ratio compressed toward 66x from last week's 67x. All eyes are on Wednesday's July CPI print (consensus: +3.4% year-on-year headline, +2.5% core): a soft reading consistent with July's payroll miss opens the path toward $4,500+ resistance and validates the summer bull run; a hot number (WTI crude surged 23.5% in the prior month) risks a sharp pullback to $4,300 support. September Fed rate-hike odds have fallen to approximately 35% from 65% a month ago, providing the macro backdrop for a sustained gold breakout if CPI cooperates.

headline: i-80 GOLD IAU Q2 2026: GRANITE CREEK TRIPLES OUTPUT TO 11,098 OZ — LONE TREE FIRST GOLD Q4, FEASIBILITY DUE Q3
snippet: i-80 Gold Corp. (TSX: IAU; NYSE: IAUX) reported Q2 2026 results on August 10, 2026, showing gold production of 11,098 ounces — a near-tripling from 4,178 ounces in Q2 2025 — with Granite Creek (Nevada) delivering a record output quarter as underground development advances ahead of schedule. The company realized an average gold price of $4,522 per ounce on gold sold. Gross profit increased to $8.6 million from $0.8 million year-over-year as the company's investment-heavy construction phase transitions into cash-generating production. The net loss widened to $52.5 million from $30.2 million as construction spending accelerated across three Nevada projects simultaneously. Cash and equivalents stood at $464.6 million as of June 30 — sufficient to fund the multi-asset development plan without dilution. Key milestones: the Granite Creek feasibility study is expected in Q3 2026, first gold from Archimedes is on track for Q4 2026, and Lone Tree mill construction is advancing. i-80 is positioning to become Nevada's next mid-tier gold producer by building an integrated multi-mine hub in the Battle Mountain Trend — one of Nevada's best-endowed gold addresses.

headline: TRIPLE COPPER SUPPLY SHOCK: DRC BANS CONCENTRATES, CHILE STORMS CUT CASERONES — LME RECORD $14,369/TONNE
snippet: Copper hit its highest level since January 2026 on August 6–8, 2026, with LME prices reaching a record $14,369.50 per tonne as three simultaneous supply shocks hit the market. First: the Democratic Republic of Congo announced a government order effective June 29 banning exports of copper and cobalt concentrates — the fourth such policy action since 2013 — triggering a 1.8% LME spike on the announcement day. Second: Category 5 storms in Chile in late July disrupted Caserones (2–3 weeks of damage to transmission infrastructure) and Los Pelambres, tightening global concentrate supply. Third: Freeport-McMoRan's Grasberg mine (Indonesia) remains at only approximately 65% of normal capacity following the September 2025 mud-rush incident, with full recovery not expected until end-2027. The DRC ban has limited near-term impact since the DRC's concentrate exports are small relative to its refined cathode exports — but the psychological overlay on top of the Chilean and Grasberg disruptions has copper bulls on the front foot. COMEX copper has separately hit a record above $6.70 per pound as U.S. tariff-driven front-loading continues. For North American copper developers, this is exactly the sustained high-price environment needed to justify the capital intensity of bringing new mines into production.

headline: TUDOR GOLD TUD.V: NEW PSP COPPER-GOLD PORPHYRY SYSTEM DISCOVERED AT TREATY CREEK, BC — 82.9m @ 0.24% CU, PSE ZONE 74.15m @ 0.78 g/t Au
source_name: Investing News Network / Tudor Gold Corp. (TSX-V: TUD)
snippet: Tudor Gold Corp. (TSX-V: TUD) announced on August 6–7, 2026 the discovery of a new copper-gold-silver-molybdenum porphyry system — named the PSP Zone — and confirmation of a distinct gold-silver epithermal system (PSE Zone) within the Perfectstorm Zone on its 80%-owned Treaty Creek Property in northwestern British Columbia's Golden Triangle. Key results from the first four drilled holes: PSP Zone hit 82.90 metres at 0.24 g/t gold, 2.11 g/t silver, 0.21% copper, and 50.76 ppm molybdenum; the best PSE Zone hole (PS-26-17) returned 74.15 metres at 0.78 g/t gold and 2.90 g/t silver over a confirmed 360-metre strike. A porphyry discovery — even with copper-dominant grades characteristic of an early-stage find — at Treaty Creek is significant context: the property already hosts the Goldstorm Deposit (over 20 million ounce gold equivalent resource) and the BCE Zone, and sits adjacent to Seabridge Gold's KSM, one of the largest undeveloped gold-copper-molybdenum systems in the world. The PSP Zone adds a third geological style of mineralization to Treaty Creek, expanding the property's exploration vectors at a moment when new copper-gold porphyry discoveries in BC are receiving heightened institutional attention.

headline: NGEX MINERALS: LUNAHUASI PHASE 4 COMPLETE — MONSTER 1,540m @ 1.17% CuEq, 15.65m @ 30.13% CuEq IN SATURN ZONE, CHILE
snippet: NGEx Minerals Ltd. (TSX-V: NGEX) reported Phase 4 drill program completion results at its Lunahuasi project in Chile on August 6, 2026, delivering the strongest results yet from what is emerging as one of the world's highest-grade copper-silver-gold systems. The headline intercept from hole DPDH064 returned a continuous 1,540.10 metres at 1.17% copper equivalent (0.79% Cu, 0.39 g/t Au, 11.3 g/t Ag), including 88.00 metres at 8.65% CuEq and a stunning 15.65 metres at 30.13% CuEq in the Saturn high-grade Zone — a grade interval that rivals the richest porphyry intersections ever drilled globally. The Phase 4 program comprised 32 holes totalling 27,318 metres, expanding the Saturn, Mars, and Jupiter zones and identifying stockwork and disseminated porphyry mineralization in new areas. Planning for Phase 5 is underway, with continued step-out drilling and testing of newly identified exploration targets. Lunahuasi is a Lundin Group-backed project in the prolific Chilean copper belt — the same geological province that hosts Escondida, Chuquicamata, and dozens of the world's largest operating copper mines — and its ultra-high-grade breccia-pipe system is the kind of discovery that drives junior-to-mid-tier re-rating events.

headline: ARTEMIS GOLD ARTG: RECORD Q2 — $285M EBITDA, $433.6M REVENUE, BLACKWATER HITS 74,063 OZ, INAUGURAL $0.05 DIVIDEND DECLARED
snippet: Artemis Gold Inc. (TSX-V: ARTG) reported record Q2 2026 financial results on August 6, 2026, headlined by record adjusted EBITDA of $285 million, record revenue of $433.6 million, and record cash flow from operations of $208 million at its wholly owned Blackwater Gold Mine in central British Columbia. Blackwater produced a quarterly record 74,063 ounces of gold in Q2 2026 — a 20% increase from Q1 — as the plant processed 1.34 million tonnes at an average grade of 1.86 g/t with 92.2% recovery (a recovery record). Year-to-date production of 135,986 ounces puts the mine on track to achieve 2026 guidance of 265,000–290,000 ounces. Adjusted net income was $199.7 million ($0.83 per share fully diluted). The board declared an inaugural quarterly dividend of $0.05 per share — payable September 9, 2026 — a milestone that signals management's confidence in sustained free cash flow generation and places Artemis in the exclusive group of profitable junior-turned-producer mines now returning capital to shareholders at current gold prices above $4,300 per ounce.

headline: B2GOLD BTO Q2: 203,648 OZ GOLD — MALI MENANKOTO PERMIT STILL PENDING, GUIDANCE CUT $50,000 OZ ON FEKOLA REGIONAL DELAY
snippet: B2Gold Corp. (TSX: BTO) released Q2 2026 results on August 6, 2026, reporting consolidated gold production of 203,648 ounces with Fekola, Masbate, and Otjikoto all outperforming internal expectations — partly offset by lower production at Goose (Nunavut, Canada) following an April 2026 crusher fire. All-in sustaining costs came in at $2,356 per ounce on gold sold. The most significant development is the ongoing delay in receiving the Menankoto Exploitation Permit from the State of Mali, which is required to begin mining the high-grade Fekola Regional satellite pits. B2Gold trimmed its full-year 2026 production guidance from 820,000–970,000 ounces to 820,000–920,000 ounces, attributing the 50,000-ounce reduction entirely to the Fekola Regional permitting delay. The company described the permit as 'expected to be issued in the near term,' but Mali's political instability and its government's increasingly assertive posture toward foreign mining companies — including the renegotiation of terms with other operators — make the timeline genuinely uncertain. For retail investors, B2Gold at current gold prices is generating substantial cash flow from its African and Asian operations even without Fekola Regional; the permit resolution represents a meaningful re-rating catalyst if and when it arrives.

headline: SILVER STORM SVRS.V LA PARRILLA: ROSARIOS ZONE 215 g/t Ag.Eq OVER 11.9m — ACTIVE MEXICO SILVER MINE WITH 93 HOLES DRILLED AND GROWING
snippet: Silver Storm Mining Ltd. (CVE: SVRS) released drill results on August 6, 2026 from its 100%-owned La Parrilla Silver Mine Complex in Durango State, Mexico — a past-producing mine now in active drill-driven resource expansion mode. The Rosarios Zone program returned Hole IDP-RO-26-004 at 215 g/t Ag.Eq over 11.90 metres and IDP-RO-26-007 at 200 g/t Ag.Eq over 15.35 metres. At silver above $65 per ounce, grades at this level represent highly economic mineralization at a mine already shipping lead-silver and zinc concentrate. The company has now completed 93 holes across the La Parrilla complex with two underground rigs and one surface rig still active, and recently expanded the 2026 drill program by 9,000 metres — a signal of management's confidence in resource growth potential. Previous results from the San Marcos Zone in July returned 1,461 g/t AgEq over 2.0 metres within 328 g/t AgEq over 15.35 metres. Silver Storm is one of very few TSX-listed companies drilling an active silver producer in Mexico in 2026, at a moment when silver above $65 and heading potentially toward triple digits (per multiple analysts) makes drill-ready Tier-2 silver systems materially more attractive than they were 12 months ago.

headline: HELIOSTAR HSTR Q2 RECORD: 14,803 OZ AU AND 79,710 OZ AG — LA COLORADA SECOND INJECTION UNIT ONLINE, 50,000 OZ GUIDANCE ON TRACK
source_name: The Globe and Mail / Heliostar Metals Ltd. (TSX-V: HSTR)
snippet: Heliostar Metals Ltd. (TSX-V: HSTR) reported Q2 2026 financial and operating results — its strongest production quarter on record — on August 6–7, 2026, achieving 14,803 ounces of gold and 79,710 ounces of silver. Year-to-date gold production of 21,940 ounces sold puts the company on track to achieve full-year guidance of 50,000–55,000 gold ounces. The operational catalyst this quarter was the commissioning of a second injection leaching unit at the La Colorada Mine in Mexico, bringing additional heap leach solution contact and increasing gold production by 49% at that operation. The San Agustin Mine maintained steady-state production. At realized gold prices above $4,300 and silver above $63 per ounce, a junior producer with a growing 50,000+ ounce gold profile and active Mexican operations is well-positioned for significant margin expansion: the 2026 gold price environment delivers roughly 2× the revenue per ounce versus the 2024 baseline. Heliostar remains in the category of small-cap producers most likely to undergo institutional re-rating if 2026H2 production meets guidance — exactly the leverage profile that outperforms in sustained gold bull markets.

headline: OROCO RESOURCE OCO.V SANTO TOMÁS: PHASE 2 INFILL CONFIRMS SOUTH ZONE EXTENDS WEST BEYOND BLOCK MODEL — 26.48m @ 1.18% CuEq
snippet: Oroco Resource Corp. (TSX-V: OCO) reported the third set of Phase 2 drill results from its Santo Tomás copper porphyry project in Sinaloa, Mexico on August 6, 2026. The batch from holes S027 and S030–S034 confirmed the high-grade South Zone extends westward beyond the boundaries of the current inferred block model in the central western portion of the deposit — an important resource expansion signal for the upcoming Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS) targeted for Q2/Q3 2027. Hole S031 delivered the third-batch headline: 26.48 metres at 1.18% copper equivalent in the South Zone. As of June 2026, Oroco had completed 22 Phase 2 holes (6,709m) across a Tier-1 Mexican copper porphyry system with a current 2024 Technical Report defining a multi-billion-pound copper resource. The Phase 2 program's systematic infill and step-out approach is methodically de-risking the block model ahead of the PFS, with each drill batch confirming or extending the 2024 resource model. Santo Tomás sits in the Sierra Madre Occidental copper belt of northern Mexico and is one of the most significant undeveloped copper porphyry projects in the Americas relative to its current market capitalization.
